tagline: Over the mountain from the coal towns to the Uintah Basin.
intro: Above Helper, near the old site of Castle Gate, US 191 leaves US 6 and heads north up Willow Creek, across the colorful country between the San Rafael Swell and the Uintah Basin. It climbs through steep rock formations and stands of conifer and aspen, over Indian Summit near the 10,000-foot level, and comes down to Duchesne.

It is an old connection. The road to Duchesne became a state highway in 1910, was moved to start at Castle Gate in 1912, and changed little before it became part of US 191 in 1981. Today it is part of the Dinosaur Diamond Prehistoric Highway.

moments.title: Castle Gate
moments.text: A coal town, dismantled in 1974, where Butch Cassidy and Elzy Lay held up a coal company employee at the railroad station in 1897 and made off with $7,000 in gold.

moments.title: Roan Cliffs
moments.text: On the east side of the Willow Creek corridor the Roan Cliffs begin, running nearly 190 miles into Colorado and less known than the Book Cliffs, being remote and inaccessible.

moments.title: Duchesne
moments.text: The Domínguez and Escalante party camped on the river just north of here in September 1776 and judged there was good land enough for three settlements.
